title: Bailey Says Nothing Suggests BOE Edging Toward a Hike
summary: “Please do not leave this room thinking that the Bank of England is edging toward a hike because there is nothing in what I said or any of us have said along those lines,” Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey tells reporters after the central bank decided to leave interest rates unchanged on Thursday. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Treasury Yields Stay Elevated After First Post-Fed Economic Data

title: Warsh Presser ‘A Little Bit Rocky,’ Says James Bullard
summary: Former St. Louis Fed President James Bullard calls the reaction in the 30-Year US Treasury to Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh’s press conference on Wednesday “nerve wracking” for a central banker. Bullard says Warsh needed to create more optionality in September and that “markets obviously didn’t like this.” (Source: Bloomberg)

title: US GDP Grows Less-Than-Expected 1.5% in Second Quarter
summary: The US economy grew at a weaker-than-expected pace in the second quarter as inflation-adjusted gross domestic product increased an annualized 1.5% in the period, despite a pickup in consumer spending and solid business investment. Michael McKee breaks down the numbers on Bloomberg Television. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: Bailey Says BOE Decided to Keep Rates at 3.75% in July
summary: Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey speaks at a news conference in London following the central bank's decision to keep interest rates unchanged in July as UK officials sought to balance the threat from resurgent US-Iran tensions against signs that domestic price pressures are easing more quickly than predicted. "We will monitor the situation carefully and stand ready to adjust our stance as the evidence and our judgements on the outlook evolve," Bailey says. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: BOE's Lombardelli Says Holding Rates Was Right Thing to Do
summary: Bank of England Deputy Governor Clare Lombardelli says her vote to hold interest rates steady at 3.75% on Thursday was not a close judgment. "I was pretty clear that holding rates at the current level was the right thing to do," she says at a press conference in London following the central bank's decision to keep rates unchanged. (Source: Bloomberg)

title: LSEG CEO Wants UK Stamp Duty on Shares to 'Go Away'
summary:
London Stock Exchange Group raised its full-year guidance after reporting its strongest first half since acquiring Refinitiv. The company said demand for its AI-powered data products continues to grow. CEO David Schwimmer also said he would "love to see" the UK's stamp duty on share purchases removed, arguing it is "the wrong incentive structure" for trading and listings. He added that the UK underinvests its own pension capital in domestic markets and sees "signs of receptivity" to reforms aimed at increasing investment. David Schwimmer joined Caroline Hepker and Stephen Carroll on Bloomberg Radio.
